```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# render from analyses/ (quarto) or project root
root <- if (file.exists("output/confirmatory_models.rds")) "." else "analyses"
res <- readRDS(file.path(root, "output/confirmatory_models.rds"))
fig_dir <- file.path(root, "figures")
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

outcome_lab <- c(peaceful = "Peaceful march", trafic = "Block traffic")
term_lab <- c(
  gini = "Gini (1 point)",
  female = "Female (ref. male)",
  civic_z = "Civic knowledge (z)",
  parents_univ = "University-educated parent",
  wave2009 = "Wave 2009 (ref. 1999)",
  wave2016 = "Wave 2016",
  wave2022 = "Wave 2022",
  `(Intercept)` = "Intercept"
)
term_order <- names(term_lab)

coef_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res), function(y) {
  bind_rows(
    res[[y]]$wemix |> mutate(model = "WeMix (weighted, primary)"),
    res[[y]]$lmer |> mutate(model = "lmer (unweighted)")
  ) |> mutate(outcome = y)
})) |>
  mutate(
    lo = estimate - 1.96 * se,
    hi = estimate + 1.96 * se,
    p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(estimate / se)),
    term_label = factor(term_lab[term], levels = term_lab[term_order]),
    outcome_label = outcome_lab[outcome]
  )

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "<.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
stars <- function(p) case_when(p < .001 ~ "***", p < .01 ~ "**", p < .05 ~ "*", TRUE ~ "")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")))
pal <- c("Peaceful march" = "#2C7FB8", "Block traffic" = "#C73E1D")
```

## Design summary

- **Outcomes** (1 = certainly not … 4 = certainly would do; ICCS items reversed to match CivED): *peaceful march* and *block traffic*.
- **Model** (preregistered): $Y_{ict} = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Gini}_{ct} + \beta_2\text{female} + \beta_3\text{civic\_z} + \beta_4\text{parents\_univ} + \gamma_t + u_c + \varepsilon_{ict}$, with a country random intercept and wave fixed effects.
- **Primary estimator**: weighted two-level model (`WeMix`), student total weights rescaled within country-wave, cluster-robust SEs. **Comparison**: unweighted `lme4::lmer`.
- Gini: SWIID v9.92 disposable-income Gini (0–100) for the survey year. Civic knowledge standardized within wave.

```{r sample}
smp <- bind_rows(lapply(res, `[[`, "sample")) |>
  mutate(outcome = outcome_lab[outcome])
kable(smp, col.names = c("Outcome", "Students", "Countries", "Country-waves"),
      format.args = list(big.mark = ","), caption = "Analytic samples (complete cases)")
```

## Main results

```{r main-table}
wide <- coef_tab |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.3f%s<br><small>[%.3f, %.3f]</small>", estimate, stars(p), lo, hi)) |>
  select(term_label, outcome_label, model, cell) |>
  mutate(col = paste(outcome_label, model, sep = " — ")) |>
  select(-outcome_label, -model) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = cell) |>
  arrange(term_label)

# variance components / ICC
icc_rows <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res), function(y) {
  r <- res[[y]]
  tau_null <- r$null_varcorr$vcov[r$null_varcorr$grp == "country"]
  sig_null <- r$null_varcorr$vcov[r$null_varcorr$grp == "Residual"]
  tau <- r$lmer_varcorr$vcov[r$lmer_varcorr$grp == "country"]
  tibble(outcome = y, icc_null = tau_null / (tau_null + sig_null), tau_cond = tau)
}))

kable(wide, escape = FALSE, col.names = c("", names(wide)[-1]),
      caption = "Fixed effects, 95% CI in brackets. * p<.05, ** p<.01, *** p<.001 (two-sided).")
```

```{r icc}
kable(icc_rows |> mutate(outcome = outcome_lab[outcome]), digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Outcome", "ICC (country, null model)", "Country variance (conditional model)"),
      caption = "Country-level variance (lmer)")
```

## Hypothesis evaluation (preregistered criteria)

Decision rule (Q7): supported if the coefficient has the expected sign and its 95% CI excludes zero; contradicted if opposite sign with CI excluding zero; otherwise inconclusive. H2 is non-directional. Evaluated on the primary (WeMix) estimates.

```{r hyp}
hyp <- tibble(
  H = c("H1", "H2", "H3", "H4"),
  term = c("gini", "female", "civic_z", "parents_univ"),
  expected = c("+", "≠ 0", "−", "+"),
  label = c("Higher inequality → more protest disposition",
            "Gender is associated with protest disposition",
            "Civic knowledge → less protest disposition",
            "University-educated parent → more protest disposition")
)
verdict <- function(est, lo, hi, expected) {
  sig <- lo > 0 | hi < 0
  case_when(
    !sig ~ "Inconclusive",
    expected == "≠ 0" ~ "Supported",
    expected == "+" & est > 0 ~ "Supported",
    expected == "−" & est < 0 ~ "Supported",
    TRUE ~ "Contradicted"
  )
}
hv <- coef_tab |>
  filter(model == "WeMix (weighted, primary)") |>
  inner_join(hyp, by = "term") |>
  mutate(
    result = verdict(estimate, lo, hi, expected),
    est = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", estimate, lo, hi)
  ) |>
  select(H, label, expected, outcome_label, est, p, result) |>
  mutate(p = fmt_p(p)) |>
  arrange(H, outcome_label)
kable(hv, col.names = c("", "Hypothesis", "Expected", "Outcome", "b [95% CI]", "p", "Result"))
```

## Prespecified robustness F: country-wave random intercept

Gini varies at the **country-wave** level. The primary model has only a country random intercept, and each country contributes thousands of students. In that setup the Gini slope is identified almost entirely by *within-country change over time*. Across country-waves, Gini has a between-country SD of about 7 points but a within-country SD of only about 1.3 points. The primary coefficient therefore does not estimate the between-country contrast stated in H1. Adding the country-wave random intercept (prespecified robustness analysis F) models the level where Gini varies. It also matches the specification of the earlier INVALSI 2022 analyses (see the reconciliation section below).

```{r cw-models}
get_tab <- function(y, nm, label) {
  t <- res[[y]][[nm]]
  if (is.null(t)) return(NULL)
  t |> mutate(outcome = y, model = label)
}
cw_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res), function(y) bind_rows(
  get_tab(y, "wemix", "Primary: country RE (WeMix)"),
  get_tab(y, "lmer_cw", "Country + country-wave RE (lmer)"),
  get_tab(y, "wemix_cw", "Country + country-wave RE (WeMix)")
))) |>
  mutate(lo = estimate - 1.96 * se, hi = estimate + 1.96 * se,
         p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(estimate / se)),
         term_label = factor(term_lab[term], levels = term_lab[term_order]),
         outcome_label = outcome_lab[outcome])

cw_wide <- cw_tab |>
  filter(term %in% c("gini", "female", "civic_z", "parents_univ")) |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.3f%s<br><small>[%.3f, %.3f]</small>", estimate, stars(p), lo, hi),
         col = paste(outcome_label, model, sep = " — ")) |>
  select(term_label, col, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = cell) |>
  arrange(term_label)
kable(cw_wide, escape = FALSE, col.names = c("", names(cw_wide)[-1]),
      caption = "Focal coefficients by random-effects structure (95% CI)")
```

```{r cw-hyp}
cw_hv <- cw_tab |>
  filter(model != "Primary: country RE (WeMix)") |>
  inner_join(hyp, by = "term") |>
  mutate(result = verdict(estimate, lo, hi, expected),
         est = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", estimate, lo, hi), p = fmt_p(p)) |>
  select(H, outcome_label, model, est, p, result) |>
  arrange(H, outcome_label, model)
kable(cw_hv, col.names = c("", "Outcome", "Model", "b [95% CI]", "p", "Result"),
      caption = "Hypothesis evaluation under robustness F")
```

## Wave-by-wave models

These are separate models per wave (country random intercept, same covariates, unweighted), comparable to the wave-specific INVALSI 2022 tables.

```{r by-wave, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
bw <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res), function(y) res[[y]]$by_wave |> mutate(outcome = y))) |>
  filter(term == "gini") |>
  mutate(lo = estimate - 1.96 * se, hi = estimate + 1.96 * se,
         outcome_label = outcome_lab[outcome])
kable(bw |> transmute(Outcome = outcome_label, Wave = study, Countries = n_countries,
                      `b Gini` = estimate, `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", lo, hi)),
      digits = 3, caption = "Gini coefficient by wave")
bwp <- ggplot(bw, aes(factor(study), estimate, color = outcome_label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = "Wave", y = "Gini coefficient (95% CI)", color = NULL)
bwp
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "gini_by_wave.png"), bwp, width = 10, height = 4.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

### Country-wave means and the Gini effect

Points are weighted country-wave means. The lines are model-implied Gini slopes anchored at the overall mean: solid for country + country-wave RE, dashed for the primary country-RE model.

```{r scatter, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
cw <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res), function(y) res[[y]]$cw_means |> mutate(outcome = y))) |>
  mutate(outcome_label = outcome_lab[outcome], wave = factor(study))
slopes <- cw_tab |> filter(term == "gini", model != "Country + country-wave RE (WeMix)") |>
  mutate(model = ifelse(grepl("Primary", model), "Country RE (primary)", "Country + country-wave RE"))
lines <- cw |>
  group_by(outcome) |>
  summarise(gmin = min(gini), gmax = max(gini), gbar = mean(gini), ybar = mean(y_mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(slopes |> select(outcome, outcome_label, model, estimate), by = "outcome") |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(outcome_label, model, gini = seq(gmin, gmax, length.out = 50),
          fit = ybar + estimate * (gini - gbar))

sp <- ggplot(cw, aes(gini, y_mean)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = wave), size = 2.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_line(data = lines, aes(gini, fit, linetype = model), linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~outcome_label, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Country + country-wave RE" = "solid", "Country RE (primary)" = "dashed")) +
  labs(x = "Gini (SWIID, disposable income)", y = "Mean disposition (1–4)", color = "Wave", linetype = NULL) +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical")
sp
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "gini_countrywave_scatter.png"), sp, width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

### Substantive size of the Gini effect

```{r size}
gsd <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res), function(y) res[[y]]$gini_cw |> mutate(outcome = y))) |>
  group_by(outcome) |>
  summarise(sd_gini = sd(gini), p10 = quantile(gini, .1), p90 = quantile(gini, .9), .groups = "drop")
sz <- cw_tab |> filter(term == "gini") |>
  left_join(gsd, by = "outcome") |>
  transmute(
    Outcome = outcome_label, Model = model,
    `Effect of +1 SD Gini` = estimate * sd_gini,
    `P10→P90 Gini` = sprintf("%.1f → %.1f", p10, p90),
    `Effect P10→P90` = estimate * (p90 - p10)
  )
kable(sz, digits = 3, caption = "Implied differences in disposition (1–4 scale)")
```

## Reconciliation with the INVALSI 2022 analyses

The INVALSI 2022 Stata models (pooled 1999–2016, radical index) reported a positive Gini effect (b ≈ 0.01, t ≈ 4.7). The table below moves step by step from that specification to the preregistered one, using the corrected pooled data (unweighted lmer, ML).

```{r reconcile}
rec_path <- file.path(root, "output/reconciliation.rds")
if (file.exists(rec_path)) {
  rec <- readRDS(rec_path)
  rec_tab <- rec$coefs |>
    filter(term == "gini") |>
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%.4f (%.4f)%s", estimate, se, stars(2 * pnorm(-abs(estimate / se))))) |>
    select(model, outcome, cell) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = outcome, values_from = cell)
  kable(rec_tab, col.names = c("Specification", "Radical index", "Block traffic", "Peaceful march", "Pacific index"),
        caption = "Gini coefficient (SE) across specifications")
}
```

- **Specification A reproduces the INVALSI result** with the corrected data (b ≈ 0.013 for the radical index).
- Adding 2022 or dropping the school level (B, C) does not change it.
- Using within-wave instead of within-country civic knowledge (D) roughly halves the effect for radical actions. Within-wave scores carry between-country knowledge differences, which correlate with Gini.
- The **sign changes only when the country-wave level is removed** (F, G). That is the random-effects structure of the preregistered primary model, and it identifies Gini from within-country change.
- Item note: the INVALSI 2016 indices used IS3G31B (*vote in national elections*) in the pacific index and IS3G31I (*volunteer time to help people*) in the radical index. The equivalent protest items are IS3G30B (*contact representative*) and IS3G30I (*spray slogans*). The indices above use the correct protest items in every wave and still reproduce the INVALSI Gini result.
- The two Gini sources are nearly identical: the INVALSI hand-coded values and SWIID v9.92 agree closely for 1999–2016.

## Notes

- Sections 2–3 report the **preregistered primary** model. The country-wave model is **prespecified robustness analysis F**. The reconciliation section is exploratory. Other robustness analyses (A–E) are pending.
- Data processing corrections made before estimation (all verified against IEA value labels): ICCS 2009/2016/2022 participation items reversed to the CivED direction; gender coding corrected for ICCS 2016 and 2022 (raw 1 = girl); valid parental-education code 0 retained; binary university indicator built per wave.
